request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our facility with incidentally detected bilateral small solid renal and adrenal masses, a cystic mass at the head of the pancreas, and a paracaval mass. The patient was diagnosed with VHL disease and staged surgical approach was recommended based on the radiologic findings.
In the first stage, through a subcostal anterior transperitoneal approach, right adrenalectomy, resection of the paracaval mass, and enucleation for the 9 small solid renal masses were performed. A Whipple procedure was also performed to remove two smaller pancreatic lesions.
In the second stage, through an intercostal extraperitoneal approach, 5 pheochromocytomas were removed and 4 cystic renal cell carcinomas were enucleated.
After a followup of 1,5 years, the patient developed a left 1 cm renal mass, which was treated by percutaneous, ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation.
Pancreatic and adrenal functions were normal throughout the follow-up period. Blood cortisol level was 21 μg/dL upon his last control visit. There was no adrenal or extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma recurrence being detected to date.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
Surgery for right adrenalectomy, resection of the paracaval mass, enucleation of small renal masses, and Whipple procedure. Followed by surgery for removal of pheochromocytomas and enucleation of cystic renal cell carcinomas. Finally, percutaneous, ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation for the left renal mass. No replacement therapy was required for pancreatic and adrenal functions.

Follow-up:
The patient will be followed up regularly for the recurrence of renal masses, pheochromocytomas, and paragangliomas. Additionally, pancreatic and adrenal functions will also be monitored.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: Q85**

The episode is best classified under von Hippel-Lindau disease, a phakomatosis, which is coded to Q85 (other phakomatoses). The multiple renal, adrenal, pancreatic, and paracaval tumours are manifestations of this single underlying genetic condition, and it is the diagnosis that was established after investigation and explains the staged surgical episode. Individual neoplasms such as the renal cell carcinomas or pheochromocytomas are secondary to it. The "Diagnosis" section is withheld, so this rests on the VHL diagnosis stated in the hospital course, and a coder would confirm it against the full record and the sequencing rules for multiple neoplasms.
